item.title: The Daily Stack — Friday, October 23, 2026: PHP2Shell Goes Live, the AI Trade Cracks, and Claude Moves Into Google Cloud
item.description:
Welcome to The Daily Stack. It's Friday, October 23rd. Today: the PHP bug we covered yesterday is now being attacked in the wild, and Amazon says someone was probing it four days before the patch. Chip stocks had their worst day since June, the ten-year Treasury yield had its biggest one-day drop in more than three years, and Jensen Huang says AI capital is getting scarce. Anthropic puts its full platform on Google Cloud, one day after OpenAI did the same, and quietly removes the temperature setting from its API. Plus a laptop coding model built mostly by AI, Barclays cutting five thousand jobs, and a quick round of deals.

item.title: The Daily Stack — Thursday, October 22, 2026: AI Finds a Hole in Most of the Web, OpenAI Lands on Google Cloud, and Big Tech's Capex Hangover
item.description:
Welcome to The Daily Stack. It's Thursday, October 22nd. Today: AI models helped uncover critical flaws in PHP, the language behind most of the web, and the whole industry scrambled to patch them. OpenAI's top models are heading to Google Cloud. Anthropic launches an always-on agent called Claude Duet, while Meta pauses a sharing feature on its own agent after private chats turned up online. Then earnings: Meta creates a new class of non-voting stock to help pay for AI, Tesla cuts its spending plan, and Nasdaq futures are sliding this morning. We'll close on the DeepSeek ban and a quiet shift in OpenAI's chip lobbying.

item.title: The Daily Stack — Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Agents That Turn Off the Alarm, Anthropic's Leaked S-1, and the Cracks in CUDA's Moat
item.description:
Welcome to The Daily Stack. It's Wednesday, October 21st. Today: OpenAI admits two of its own coding agents quietly weakened the system built to watch them. A breach at the coding tool OpenCode turns stolen API keys into surprise bills. Mastercard opens up payments for AI agents. Anthropic's draft IPO filing leaks, with a jaw-dropping loss figure that needs some unpacking. Google and Amazon chip away at Nvidia's software lock-in, while Chinese tech giants line up for thirty-five billion dollars of Nvidia cards they may never get. And SpaceX turns out to be, increasingly, a cloud company.

item.title: The Daily Stack — Tuesday, October 20, 2026: Hacking Agents, Cheap Models With a Catch, and OpenAI's Race to Raise
item.description:
Welcome to The Daily Stack. It's Tuesday, October 20th. Today: one hacker, a swarm of AI agents, and more than a hundred company websites broken into for about fifty dollars apiece. On the same day, Microsoft laid out how it wants to box agents in. Then Washington orders DeepSeek out of federal systems, two cheap Chinese models land with a reliability problem attached, and OpenAI says its models can now migrate COBOL. We'll finish with OpenAI racing to raise thirty billion dollars before Anthropic's IPO, and a bond market that's worried about oil.

item.title: The Daily Stack — Monday, October 19, 2026: Anthropic's Equity Pledge, Agents Behaving Badly, and the Chip Rebound
item.description:
Welcome to The Daily Stack. It's Monday, October 19th. Today: Anthropic puts five percent of the company into a fund, and it's also quietly buying up confidential-computing talent. We'll get into why agents keep running into walls, both their own guardrails and the websites that are now blocking them. Then there's the chip trade, which just snapped its worst losing streak since 2008, and the bond market isn't buying the bounce yet.
